questions.question: Hai - Hak Dance is associated with which state?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Tripura.

Key Points

    • It is a folk dance performed by the Malsum community, one of the many indigenous communities of the state.
    • The dance is typically performed after the harvesting season to thank Goddess Laxmi for the bountiful crop.
    • The Hai-Hak Dance is a group dance performed by both men and women.
    • The dancers wear traditional costumes and jewelry, and the dance is accompanied by the beat of drums and other musical instruments.
    • The dance movements are energetic and expressive, and they depict the joy and gratitude of the community for the harvest.

questions.question: Which among the following dances is also known as Ekaharya, where one dancer takes on many roles in a single performance?
questions.questionHtml: Which among the following dances is also known as Ekaharya, where one dancer takes on many roles in a single performance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bharatnatyam.

Key Points

  • Bharatnatyam is the oldest Indian classical dance 
  • It originated hundreds of years ago in the state of Tamilnadu.
  • This dance form expresses the religious themes and spiritual ideas of South India.
  • The ancient Tamil epic Silappatikaram contains the description of Bharatnatyam.

Additional Information

  • The Sangeet Natak academy currently confers classical status on eight Indian classical dance styles:
Dance  Originates
Bharatnatyam  Tamilnadu
Kathak (North, West and Central India) 
Kathakali Kerela
Kuchipudi Andhra Pradesh
Odissi Odisha
Manipuri Manipur
Mohiniattam Kerela
Sattriya Assam

Important Points

  • Sangeet Natak Academy (India’s National Academy) recognizes only eight classical dances of India, however, the Ministry of Culture also considers Chhau Dance as a classical dance of India, making the total number of classical dances in India as nine.

questions.question: Deba Prasad Das, Pankaj Charan Das and Gangadhar Pradhan are associated with which of the following dance forms?
questions.questionHtml: Deba Prasad Das, Pankaj Charan Das and Gangadhar Pradhan are associated with which of the following dance forms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Odissi

Key Points

  • Deba Prasad Das, Pankaj Charan Das, and Gangadhar Pradhan are renowned figures associated with the Odissi dance form.
  • Odissi is one of the classical dance forms of India, originating from the state of Odisha.
  • This dance form is known for its fluid movements, grace, and intricate gestures, often depicting religious stories and spiritual themes.
  • Odissi has a rich history and has been traditionally performed in temples as a form of worship.

Additional Information

  • Deba Prasad Das is considered one of the founding fathers of modern Odissi dance and has contributed significantly to its revival and popularization.
  • Pankaj Charan Das was a legendary guru and choreographer who played a crucial role in shaping the Odissi dance form.
  • Gangadhar Pradhan was a prominent Odissi dancer and guru known for his dedication to promoting and preserving this classical dance form.
  • Odissi is characterized by its use of tribhangi (three bends of the body) and chowk (a square-like stance), which are fundamental to its technique.

questions.question: Uma Sharma was conferred the Padma Bhushan award for enriching which of the following forms of Classical Dances in India?
questions.questionHtml: Uma Sharma was conferred the Padma Bhushan award for enriching which of the following forms of Classical Dances in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kathak.

Key Points

  • Uma Sharma has been conferred the Padma Bhushan award for enriching Kathak form of Classical Dances in India.
  • She was also bestowed with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award and also the Sahitya Kala Parishad Award. Sharma has also been honoured with the “Srijan Manishi” title by Akhil Bhartiya Vikram Parishad for her great contribution to Kathak.
  • Uma Sharma (born 1942) is a Kathak dancer, choreographer, and teacher. She also runs the Bharatiya Sangeet Sadan, Delhi, a classical dance and music academy, situated in New Delhi, founded by her father in 1946.
  • In 1973 she became the youngest dancer to be conferred with the Padma Shri by the Government of India, and Padma Bhushan 2001.

Additional Information

  • The world-famous Kathak dancer, Pandit Birju Maharaj is the face of the Kalka-Bindadin Gharana of Lucknow.
  • Kathak, a north Indian dance form, is a mixture of dance and drama which is usually performed by both men and women.
  • Venkatalakshamma (29 May 1906 – 1 July 2002) was a renowned Bharatanatyam dancer. A doyenne of the Mysore Style of Bharatanatyam.
  • Savitha Sastry (born 11 December 1969) is an Indian dancer and choreographer best known as an exponent of Bharatanatyam.
  • Konsam Ibomcha Singh was awarded the Padma Shri in recognition of his distinguished services in Arts, of preserving the century-old dying art of Laiphadabi (doll) making of the Meitei community in Manipur.

questions.question: Which of the following dance forms traces its lineage to the ancient dance of Sadir Attam?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following dance forms traces its lineage to the ancient dance of Sadir Attam?
questions.solution: Bharatanatyam traces its lineage back to the ancient dance form of Sadir Attam, evolving into a sophisticated performance art with a rich blend of expressions, music, and storytelling deeply rooted in Tamil Nadu's tradition. On the other hand, Kuchipudi is a classical dance from Andhra Pradesh known for its graceful movements and strong narrative character. Mohiniyattam, originating from Kerala, is characterized by its gentle, lyrical motions and feminine elegance. Kathakali, also from Kerala, stands out with its elaborate costumes, detailed gestures, and facial expressions, telling stories from Hindu epics and Puranas. Each dance form, while distinct, contributes to India's diverse cultural tapestry.

questions.question: The ‘Veeragase’ dance, performed during the Dusshera festival holds a special place in the folk dances of the state of ______.
questions.questionHtml: The ‘Veeragase’ dance, performed during the Dusshera festival holds a special place in the folk dances of the state of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Karnataka.

Key Points

  • Veeragase is the dance form of Karnataka.
  • It is a vigorous dance based on Hindu mythology and includes very aggressive energy-sapping dance movements performed by the Jangama.
  • It is one of the dances seen in the Dasara procession that took place in Mysore.
  • This dance is done at festivals and often during Shravana and Karthika's Hindu months.
  • It is carried out on all essential Lingayat functions.​

Additional Information

  • Sikkim:
    • Chu-Faat: The meaning of Chu is the Snowy Range and that of Faat is Worship.
    • It is a group folk dance of Sikkim performed in honour of Mount Khangchendzonga.
  • Odisha:
    • Chhau Dance is a traditional dance form of Odisha.
    • It is found in three styles named after the place where they are performed, i.e. Bengal's Purulia Chau, Jharkhand's Seraikella Chau, and Odisha's Mayurbhanj Chau.
    • The dance ranges from celebrating martial arts, acrobatics, and athletics performed in folk dance festive themes, to a formal dance with religious themes found in Shaivism, Shaktism, and Vaishnavism.
    • The costumes vary from one style to another, with Purulia and Serakeilla using masks to identify characters.
    • The tales of Chhau dancers include those from the Hindu epics of Ramayana and Mahabharata, Puranas, and other Indian literature.
  • Assam:

  • He won Padma Shri Award in the year 1972 and the Sangeet Natak Academy Award in 1966.
  • In 1989, he became the proud winner of the Padma Bhushan Award. 
  • He was honoured with the Sangeet Academy Fellowship in 1991.
  • Again, in the year 2000, he was awarded the highly remarkable Padma Vibhushan Award.
  • The government of Madhya Pradesh honoured him with the Kalidas Samman too.

Additional Information

  • Nileshwar Mukherjee, Bipin Singh, and Haricharan Singh were famous Manipuri dancer.
  • The Sangeet Natak Academy recognizes eight – Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Kathakali, Sattriya, Manipuri, and Mohiniyattam.  
  • Sangeet Natak Akademi – India’s national academy of music, dance, and drama – is the first national academy of the arts set up by the Republic of India. It was created by a resolution of the (then) Ministry of Education, Government of India, dated 31 May 1952, which was notified in the Gazette of India of June 1952.

questions.question: Which of the following communities of Sikkim is traditionally associated with the folk dance known as 'Chu-Faat'?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following communities of Sikkim is traditionally associated with the folk dance known as 'Chu-Faat'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Lepcha.

Key Points

  • Lepcha communities of Sikkim are traditionally associated with the folk dance known as 'Chu-Faat'.
  • Chu-Faat:
    • The meaning of Chu is the Snowy Range and that of Faat is Worship.
    • It is a group folk dance of Sikkim performed in honour of Mount Khangchendzonga.
  • Lepcha communities:
    • About 45,000 Lepchas live in the high mountain valleys of Sikkim, a north Indian state, particularly in an area called the Dzongu Lepcha Reserve, near Mount Kanchenjunga, the world's third-highest mountain.
    • Some Lepchas also live in Kalimpong, West Bengal, plus neighbouring Bhutan and Nepal.
    • The Tholung Monastery, a well-known trekking destination in the Dzongu Reserve, was extensively damaged by an earthquake in September 2011.
    • The Lepchas raise a variety of crops-maize (corn), rice, cardamom, and garden vegetables and they keep goats, cattle, and pigs.
    • The Lepcha culture suppresses aggression and competition almost completely.

questions.question: Paika dance of Jharkhand is usually performed by the __________ tribe to welcome special honoured guests or during religious processions (Shobha Yatra).
questions.questionHtml: Paika dance of Jharkhand is usually performed by the __________ tribe to welcome special honoured guests or during religious processions (Shobha Yatra).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 2) Munda

Key Points

  • Paika dance is a traditional dance form of Jharkhand.
  • It is usually performed by the Munda tribe to welcome special honoured guests or during religious processions (Shobha Yatra).
  • The dance is a form of martial art and involves vigorous movements and use of traditional weapons.
  • The dancers wear traditional attire and headgear, adding to the visual appeal of the performance.
  • Paika dance is not only a form of entertainment but also a way to showcase the valor and martial skills of the tribe.

Additional Information

  • The Santhal, Oraon, and Bhumij tribes also have their own unique dance forms and cultural practices.
  • Jharkhand is known for its rich cultural heritage and diverse tribal traditions.
  • The state celebrates various festivals where traditional dances like Paika are performed to mark the occasion.
  • Efforts are being made to preserve and promote these traditional art forms through cultural festivals and government initiatives.

questions.question: Consider the following statements in context to Dollu Kunitha dance. Select the correct statements. a) It is a popular dance of Karnataka. b) Drums are adorned with colourful clothes. c) Religious and battle fervor songs are sung.
questions.questionHtml:
Consider the following statements in context to Dollu Kunitha dance. Select the correct statements.

a) It is a popular dance of Karnataka.

b) Drums are adorned with colourful clothes.

c) Religious and battle fervor songs are sung.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is a, b, c.

Key Points

  • Dollu Kunitha:-
    • It is a traditional dance form of Karnataka, performed mainly by the menfolk of the shepherd community.
    • The word "Dollu" means "drum" in Kannada, and the dance is characterized by the use of large drums, which are decorated with colorful clothes and played by the dancers themselves.
    • The dance is usually performed during religious festivals and other auspicious occasions, and is accompanied by songs that are sung in praise of gods and goddesses, as well as in celebration of battles and victories.

questions.solution: Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (Akademi Puraskar) for the year 2020 was awarded to Meenakshi Chitharanjan for her contribution to Bharatanatyam.

questions.question: Which of the following classical dance forms of India is a blend of dance, music and acting and dramatises stories, which are mostly adapted from the Indian epics?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following classical dance forms of India is a blend of dance, music and acting and dramatises stories, which are mostly adapted from the Indian epics?
questions.solution: Kathakali is a classical Indian dance form that integrates dance, music, and acting to dramatize stories from Indian epics like the Mahabharata and Ramayana. Originating in Kerala, it features elaborate costumes, intricate makeup, and detailed gestures. Performances usually take place in the evenings and can extend for several hours. Kathakali combines elements of literature, music, painting, and acting, making it a comprehensive art form. In contrast, Manipuri, Odissi, and Kathak are other classical dance forms from different regions of India, each with its unique style, themes, and cultural significance.

questions.question: _______ is a traditional tribal dance performed mainly by the women of Jharkhand during the cultivation season.
questions.questionHtml: _______ is a traditional tribal dance performed mainly by the women of Jharkhand during the cultivation season.
questions.solution: Jhumur is a traditional tribal dance of Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Bihar, and West Bengal. It is performed by women during the cultivation season. The dance has its roots in the Sadan community of Chotanagpur. The musical instruments used in Jhumur are Mandar, Dhol, Nagara, and Bansuri. It is a celebration of the harvest season and is an integral part of the tribal culture of the region.

questions.question: Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma is known to create the format structure and ornamentation of the _____ dance form.
questions.questionHtml: Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma is known to create the format structure and ornamentation of the _____ dance form.
questions.solution: Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma is a renowned dancer and choreographer from Kerala, India. She is known for her contributions to the development and popularization of the Mohiniyattam dance form, which originated in Kerala.

questions.question: Shovana Narayan is a renowned __________ dancer.
questions.questionHtml: Shovana Narayan is a renowned __________ dancer.
questions.solution: Shovana Narayan is a renowned Kathak dancer, which is a classical dance form originating from northern India. Kathak dance form is known for its intricate footwork, rhythmic body movements, and facial expressions. Shovana Narayan has received several accolades for her contribution to the field of dance, including the Padma Shri and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

questions.question: Rabindra Sangeet is a set of folk songs sung during festivals and rituals in ________.
questions.questionHtml: Rabindra Sangeet is a set of folk songs sung during festivals and rituals in ________.
questions.solution:
• Rabindra Sangeet is a set of folk songs sung in West Bengal.

questions.question: Who among the following continues to be hailed as the empress of Bharatanatyam across the world?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following continues to be hailed as the empress of Bharatanatyam across the world?
questions.solution: Tanjore Balasaraswati is considered one of the greatest Bharatanatyam dancers of all time. She was born in 1918 in Tamil Nadu and began her training in Bharatanatyam at a young age. Balasaraswati was known for her grace, fluidity, and emotive performances, and was a major force in popularizing Bharatanatyam both in India and abroad.

questions.question: Who was conferred with the National Nritya Shiromani Award 2022?
questions.questionHtml: Who was conferred with the National Nritya Shiromani Award 2022?
questions.solution: Aparna Satheesan was conferred with the National Nritya Shiromani Award 2022 for her exceptional contribution to classical dance. She is an international Kuchipudi dancer from Kerala and an expert in Bharatnatyam. She received the award at the 13th Cuttak Mahotsav. Kuchipudi is one of the 8 major Indian classical dances and originated from Andhra Pradesh while Bharatnatyam originated from Tamil Nadu.

questions.question: Who among the following was the first woman classical dancer in independent India to be nominated as a member to the Rajya Sabha?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following was the first woman classical dancer in independent India to be nominated as a member to the Rajya Sabha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Rukmini Devi Arundale.​Key Points

  • Rukmini Devi Arundale was an Indian theosophist, dancer and choreographer of the Indian classical dance form of Bharatanatyam, and an activist for animal welfare.
  • She was the first woman in Indian history to be nominated as a member of the Rajya Sabha, the upper house of the Parliament of India.
  • Rukmini Devi, founder of Kalakshetra, is credited with giving Bharatanatyam makeover from sensuous art form to more spiritual & devotional .

Additional Information

  • Vidyagauri Adkar is a Kathak dance exponent in India representing the Jaipur gharana. She has performed in many music festivals including Khajuraho Festival of Dances, Chilanka Dance Festival in Thiruvananthapuram, Festival of Dance and Music, Delhi etc.
  • Niveditha Arjun is an Indian actress, producer and dancer.
  • Kalamandalam Kallyanikutty Amma was an epoch-making Mohiniyattam danseuse from Kerala in southern India.
